prerequisites: Competences from previous semesters, especially Materials Science and Engineering
Elasticity and Strength of Materials I

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to fluently use computer at user level.
Apply knowledge professionally to work or vocation and demonstrate competences through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem solving within the area of study.
Transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Knowledge and abilities for the application of materials engineering in industrial environments.
Aptitude for oral and written communication in the native language.
Developed learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to manage mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling learning of new methods and theories and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Competence in the sustainable use of resources and in the prevention of negative impacts on the natural and social environment.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK 1: INTRODUCTION - Materials Engineering and Technology.
BLOCK 2: MATERIALS OF INDUSTRIAL INTEREST - Ferrous alloys: steels and cast irons.
BLOCK 2: MATERIALS OF INDUSTRIAL INTEREST - Non-ferrous alloys: Light alloys, common alloys and special alloys.
BLOCK 2: MATERIALS OF INDUSTRIAL INTEREST - Ceramics and Glasses.
BLOCK 2: MATERIALS OF INDUSTRIAL INTEREST - Polymers.
BLOCK 2: MATERIALS OF INDUSTRIAL INTEREST - Composite Materials.
BLOCK 3: MECHANICAL AND IN-SERVICE BEHAVIOR OF MATERIALS - Mechanical properties.
BLOCK 3: MECHANICAL AND IN-SERVICE BEHAVIOR OF MATERIALS - Fracture.
BLOCK 3: MECHANICAL AND IN-SERVICE BEHAVIOR OF MATERIALS - Fatigue.
BLOCK 3: MECHANICAL AND IN-SERVICE BEHAVIOR OF MATERIALS - Creep.
BLOCK 3: MECHANICAL AND IN-SERVICE BEHAVIOR OF MATERIALS - Wear in materials.
BLOCK 3: MECHANICAL AND IN-SERVICE BEHAVIOR OF MATERIALS - Corrosion and oxidation.
BLOCK 4: MATERIALS TECHNOLOGY - Surface treatments.
BLOCK 4: MATERIALS TECHNOLOGY - Material joining techniques.
BLOCK 5: MATERIALS CHARACTERIZATION AND FAILURE ANALYSIS - Non-destructive testing.
BLOCK 5: MATERIALS CHARACTERIZATION AND FAILURE ANALYSIS - Methodology for materials failure analysis.
BLOCK 6: MATERIAL AND PROCESS SELECTION IN INDUSTRY - Material selection process.
BLOCK 6: MATERIAL AND PROCESS SELECTION IN INDUSTRY - Property control and manipulation.
BLOCK 6: MATERIAL AND PROCESS SELECTION IN INDUSTRY - Case studies.

LABORATORY PRACTICES: Resolution of industrial-focused practical cases for material quality control validation, including the performance of the following tests: 1- Non-destructive tests: ultrasonics.

LABORATORY PRACTICES: Resolution of industrial-focused practical cases for material quality control validation, including the performance of the following tests: 2- Jominy end-quench test for steel hardenability.

LABORATORY PRACTICES: Resolution of industrial-focused practical cases for material quality control validation, including the performance of the following tests: 3- Susceptibility to intergranular corrosion of aluminum alloys.
teaching_methods: Workshop/laboratory practices (performing tests under standards, practical case studies, autonomous lab time management, cooperative learning)
Non-contact learning activities (prior readings, vocabulary preparation, individual problem solving, lab practice preparation, resolution of proposed activities, questionnaires/reports)
Personalized and group tutoring (in-person and virtual), consultation forums
Lectures (expository method/master class, structured topic presentation, virtual classroom support, CLIL activity in English)

Problem-solving practices and seminars (exercise and problem solving, application of formulas/algorithms/procedures, interpretation of results, material selection case resolution, autonomous development with professor's guidance)

assessment_methods.method: Progress tests and/or final exam (tests with different sections: multiple choice, short answer questions, problems, and practical cases to evaluate acquired knowledge)
Oral/written evaluation of laboratory practices (covering theoretical content and practical execution)
Resolution of practical material selection cases (using specific software/databases, integrating acquired knowledge)
